title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned a product-packaging world. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Label Stock
options.thesis: The whole company profile is a product package: a label you can read, a barcode you can scan, and a box you can open.
options.viewport: A product label as the first viewport: brand name as product name, services as contents, a barcode rail and a 'contact customer service' seal.
options.risk: Reads as a novelty skin if the label grammar stops at the hero instead of carrying through every section.

raised.raise: Each service is a labeled package on a shelf the visitor can open, not a card in a grid.
Every section carries the same diagnostic labels (batch, contents, weight) so the eye cross-checks instead of re-reading.
Headlines are set as product names with real weight, never as display fluff.
Anything not on hand is marked 'out of stock' honestly instead of being hidden or fabricated.

options.label: Morning Paper
options.thesis: The studio presented as a daily paper: a masthead, a front page, and columns a business owner trusts.
options.viewport: A masthead first viewport with the company name as the paper's name, the offer as the headline story, and contact as the 'letters to the editor' rail.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category land on: a newsroom skin is familiar and effective, and you are choosing that trade.

options.label: Civic Bureau
options.thesis: A prospectus for a public body: bone-white plates, a violet ribbon of colour, and a lacquered object that proves the work.
options.viewport: A 48/52 split: the argument in two weights of one face on the left, a WebGL ribbon and a lacquered console on the right, a 72px sticky bar above.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: services map to council bands, portfolio to case files. Wins on B2B audience identification and prospectus clarity.
options.risk: Reads as a generic SaaS prospectus if the ribbon and the lacquered object are dropped to accents.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: The studio's work traced as a red silk ribbon through time: every project a dated fold, every gap shown as unwoven thread.
options.viewport: A single ribbon-led column: dated custody folds, geographic movement, and gaps rendered as gray unwoven thread.
options.case: Holds product clarity via transparent process; loses audience (museum register against a business owner).
options.risk: Reads as an exhibition label if the ribbon becomes decoration.

options.label: Highlife Sleeve
options.thesis: The studio as a bandleader's sleeve: a grinning portrait under an arced hand-brushed name, in mango and palm green.
options.viewport: An arced hand-brushed band name over a cut-out portrait, with track lists as services below.
options.case: Holds audience identification via Indonesian tropical warmth; loses product clarity (music sleeve against service catalog).
options.risk: Reads as a novelty poster if the arced type is set timidly.

options.label: Minihompy Room
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful furnishing reads as a toy, not B2B credibility.
options.kept: Identity as a space visitors can enter and furnish.

options.label: Night Flight Six-Pack
options.case: Fuses poorly: an instrument panel reads as cockpit cosplay for an agency.
options.kept: Cross-check reading order across a fixed constellation.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.case: Fuses poorly: surreal weather erases service clarity.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably: a clean grid, real product photography, and a visitor who knows exactly where to click.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft: hero, three services, three portfolio items, CTA.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
